title: Vegetable Frittata
subtitle: Italian baked omelette with peppers, courgette, and parmesan
excerpt: A frittata is a thick Italian egg dish that starts on the hob and finishes in the oven. It is good hot, warm, or cold and keeps well in the fridge for two days.
sourceNotes: Classic Italian frittata method. The hob-to-oven approach gives a set top without flipping.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook up to 2 days ahead. Serve at room temperature or briefly warm under the grill.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 180 or gas 6. For finishing in the oven.

content.text: Use an ovenproof frying pan so it can go straight from the hob into the oven. The frittata is ready when the centre no longer wobbles.
Heat the oven to 200 degrees C.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl. Stir in the parmesan, chives, and a generous pinch of salt.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof frying pan over medium heat. Add the pepper and courgette. Cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and spinach. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Spread the vegetables evenly across the pan.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables. Cook on the hob for 3 minutes until the edges start to set.
Transfer to the oven. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the centre is just set and no longer wobbles.
Leave to cool for 5 minutes. Slide onto a board and cut into wedges to serve.

items.symptom: Centre is still runny after 12 minutes in the oven.
items.cause: Pan was very cold going in or egg layer was thick.
items.fix: Return for 3 to 5 more minutes; cover loosely with foil if the top colours too fast.

items.symptom: Frittata sticks badly to the pan.
items.cause: Not enough oil or pan was not non-stick.
items.fix: Use a well-seasoned or non-stick ovenproof pan; oil the sides too.

items.symptom: Vegetables released too much liquid into the eggs.
items.cause: Courgette or spinach not cooked enough before eggs went in.
items.fix: Cook vegetables until any liquid evaporates before pouring in eggs.
